subtype: Approach: minimise the EMI only, ignoring total interest [Pitfall]
passage: Sunday night, four years on. I opened the loan statement today because Harish asked how much I had paid so far. Total paid: a lot. Principal reduced: not much. Back when I signed, I stretched the repayment to the longest period so the monthly instalment felt light, and I could still buy things and travel. It made the first year very comfortable. But the statement shows how much interest I am adding every month, and when I added it up, it was more than a third of what I borrowed. Harish said gently that a lower instalment eases today but costs more later. I wish I had done that sum at the start. Arnab

qa.q: Who asked Arnab how much had been paid so far?
qa.a: Harish asked how much had been paid so far.

qa.q: What did Arnab feel when adding up the interest?
qa.a: Arnab felt regret, wishing the sum had been done at the start.

qa.q: What could Arnab do next about the loan, and why?
qa.a: Arnab could ask the bank what options exist for paying more or shortening the term, because the interest depends on how long the balance stays.

qa.q: How might Harish see the choice of the longest period?
qa.a: Harish sees that it eased the early years but cost more later, and told Arnab so gently.

grounding: A borrower stretches the tenure to the maximum so the instalment feels small, and only years later notices the total interest has grown.
